title: Can it be opened?
description:
Write `try_open(path)`: it opens the zero-terminated path read-only with system call 2. If that works, it closes the file again and returns 0; if not, it returns the negative error number the kernel gave.

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `try_open("/")` | 0 (a folder can be opened for reading) |
| `try_open("/no/such/file")` | −2 (no such file) |

solution.solution.asm:
try_open:
        mov     eax, 2                  ; open(path, O_RDONLY)
        xor     esi, esi
        xor     edx, edx
        syscall
        test    rax, rax
        js      .done                   ; negative: give the error back
        mov     rdi, rax
        mov     eax, 3                  ; close(fd)
        syscall
        xor     eax, eax
.done:  ret

hints: `rdi` already holds the path when the function starts, which is exactly where `open` wants it. Only `rax` (2) and the flags in `rsi` (0) need setting.
